thread.title_full: Royal Weber a Constant Force for Shiloh's Stout Defense - NewsBreak

author: Jerell Rushin
title: Royal Weber a Constant Force for Shiloh's Stout Defense - NewsBreak
text:
By Jerell Rushin ,
4 hours ago Shiloh's Royal Weber (22) closes in on a tackle during a football game against Tri-Cities on Sept. 19, 2025. By Vincent Myers There’s a constant at Shiloh football that stands out like the pink mouth pieces players paired with their silver-trimmed black and white uniforms during its 14-7 win at Decatur earlier this season.
Senior linebacker Royal Weber is one of the most impressive Generals each game, logging turnovers and tackles for loss as a force of habit. He made two of the biggest plays of the game against Decatur.
Shiloh was scoreless since early second quarter but led 14-0 as the third quarter closed. On fourth-and-inches in Shiloh territory, running back Sadur Salahuddin was on path for a Decatur conversion. Weber dashed in at the final moment, met him at the line of scrimmage and churned and dug his feet for the turnover on downs tackle.
Shiloh, ravished by four defensive starters injuries during the second half that, finally allowed a touchdown and punted to Decatur with under three minutes left. The punt ricocheted off a Decatur player’s helmet, and resourceful Weber was closest to the loose ball, grabbed it and gave up himself.
As the three-year starter with 16 FBS and FCS offers reached the sideline, a teammate yelled towards him, “I love you, man!” The offense gained two first downs from there to clinch Shiloh’s third straight win. Weber finished with multiple sacks and tackles for loss.
“You can’t play like a bot,” Weber said. “You have to fly around. I was going to try and scoop and score, but my teammate was right there. It was best to get the ball right here and let the offense run out the clock. That’s really my motive — fly around, play with speed, keep your mind right.”
Weber, 6-foot-2 and 210 pounds, had two interceptions, one returned over 60 yards for a touchdown, in a 49-0 win over region for Tri-Cities. He owns command of his defense, calling adjustments and directions during pre-play. He entered this week with 61 tackles (12 for losses), three sacks, four quarterback hurries and two interceptions.
Weber has improved leaps since working with first-year linebacker coach Isaac Dowling, an FCS freshman All-American linebacker at Mercer, coach Tino Ierulli said.
Weber has taken an official visit to Kennesaw State, and also holds offers from Georgia State, UAB, Army, Navy, Missouri State and UT-Martin. He’s planning a Nov. 22 gameday visit to Kennesaw State and to take more official visits in December.
“He’s fast, physical, he’s strong,” Ierulli said. “He’s still got a frame where you can put 25 to 35 pounds of muscle on him and still keep his speed. He’s what you want in a college linebacker. He’s got the length, the speed, the aggression, the strength and the football IQ.”
Weber hasn’t received a Power 4 offer, and Dowling tells his linebacker to focus on his growth and schooling. He has much more potential to realize, and is taking his senior season week-by-week to capitalize on it, Weber said.
“He’s sideline to sideline,” Dowling said. “You can’t teach his natural speed and getting off the ball, making plays. He’s learning every day. Every week he’s been reading pulls, reading formations. It’s been good. I can see him definitely being a D-I linebacker, and also a P4.
“He’s got the size, he’s got the speed. He's just got to continue working. I tell him all the time don’t worry about the offers too much. They look good and everything, but we’ve got to focus on what needs to be done on the field and in the classroom as well. But he’s improving every week. I expect him to blow up this offseason. I’m ready to see that.”
